title: Example 18-10: Linear Diagram with a Vertical Line

illustrates.quote: Linear Diagrams with Print Symbols. Follow print for use of the appropriate sign and spacing to show separate parts of a sentence. List these symbols on the Special Symbols page, or in a transcriber’s note before the text.

blocks.text: The boy | played in the park.

print.notes: The vertical line "|" is an ordinary UEB print symbol (dots 456, 1256) — translates correctly with zero Emboss-specific code. The required 1-3 margin (18.7.1, shared by every linear diagram) cannot be produced (F-189); an ordinary paragraph block’s own default indent is used instead — expected mismatch on indent only.
print.printFeatures: Sentence containing a vertical line, enclosed in a box (the box itself: F-189, no diagram/box wrapper exists for this content).

braille.notes: Re-extracted from source (line 14647, margin 9); matches both runs byte-for-byte.

resolution: Braille already agreed and re-extraction confirms it exactly. The sentence forward-translates to the given braille exactly at zero indent; built as a plain paragraph, with the required 1-3 margin recorded as the expected F-189 mismatch cause rather than guessed at with an unsupported block option. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.evidence: Page image references/_gemini/_done/gold-18-A/page-505.png (Example 18-10): the one-line diagram 'The boy | played in the park.' starts flush at the box margin with no paragraph indent (contrast the indented first paragraph of Example 18-9 above it).

Page image references/_gemini/_done/gold-18-A/page-505.png: Example 18-10 is titled 'Linear Diagram with a Vertical Line' under 18.7.2; the print is a one-line sentence diagram ('The boy | played in the park.') whose parts are separated by a vertical line; 18.7.1 on page-504.png says to use 1-3 margins for each diagrammed sentence.
